look at random forests for variable importance by species
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ranger)
library(ggplot2)
library(glue)
library(ggcorrplot)


# Define predictors
predictors <- c(  'MCMT', 'CMD_sm', 'SHM',   'PAS_an',
             'DD18_an',  'MAT', 'DDsub0_sp', 'Eref_an', 
             'Tmin_sm')#'AHM','EXT','bFFP',"MAP",'DD5_an',, 'Tmax_sm''CMI_an',

# Preprocess
assessed.rf <- assessed %>%
  filter(PERIOD == "1961_1990") %>%
  select(survival, species, PERIOD, all_of(predictors)) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(
    survival = round(survival * 100, 0),
    species = as.factor(species)
  )
assessed.rf <- assessed.rf %>%
  mutate(
    # 📉 CMD_sm: Strong right skew — log-transform
    CMD_sm = log(CMD_sm + 1),

    # 📊 DD18_an: Low variance, clustered — center and scale
    DD18_an = scale(DD18_an),

    # 📊 DDsub0_sp: Multimodal and skewed — log-transform
    DDsub0_sp = log(DDsub0_sp + 1),

    # 🌡️ Eref_an: Long tail — log-transform
    Eref_an = log(Eref_an + 1),

    # 🌡️ MAT: Slight skew — center and scale
    MAT = scale(MAT),

    # 🌡️ MCMT: Slight skew — center and scale
    MCMT = scale(MCMT),

    # 🌧️ PAS_an: Strong right skew — log-transform
    PAS_an = log(PAS_an + 1),

    # 🌡️ SHM: Slight skew — center and scale
    SHM = scale(SHM),

    # 🌡️ Tmin_sm: Low variance — center and scale
    Tmin_sm = scale(Tmin_sm)
  )
# Reshape to long format
assessed.rf.long <- assessed.rf %>%
  select(all_of(predictors)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value")

# Plot histograms
ggplot(assessed.rf.long, aes(x = Value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Histograms of Climate Predictors (1961–1990)",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
# Compute correlation matrix
cor_df <- assessed %>%
  filter(PERIOD == "1961_1990") %>%
  select(all_of(predictors)) %>%
  drop_na()

cor_matrix <- cor(cor_df, method = "pearson")

# Plot using ggcorrplot
ggcorrplot(cor_matrix,
           hc.order = TRUE,
           type = "lower",
           lab = TRUE,
           lab_size = 3,
           colors = c("blue", "white", "red"),
           title = "Correlation Matrix of Climate Predictors",
           ggtheme = theme_minimal())

# Remove highly correlated variables globally
remove_high_corr <- function(df, cutoff = 0.9) {
  df <- df %>% select(-survival, -species, -PERIOD)
  cor_matrix <- cor(df)
  cor_pairs <- which(abs(cor_matrix) > cutoff & lower.tri(cor_matrix), arr.ind = TRUE)
  to_remove <- unique(rownames(cor_matrix)[cor_pairs[, 2]])
  df %>% select(-all_of(to_remove))
}
```


```{r}
# Apply correlation filtering
filtered_predictors <- remove_high_corr(assessed.rf)
assessed.rf2 <- assessed.rf %>%
  select(survival, species, PERIOD) %>%
  bind_cols(filtered_predictors)

# Split by species
species_list <- split(assessed.rf2, assessed.rf2$species)

# Fit RF models
rf_models <- imap(species_list, function(df, sp) {
  if (ncol(df) <= 2) {
    message(glue("Skipping species '{sp}' — no predictors left after correlation filtering."))
    return(NULL)
  }
  ranger(
    survival ~ .,
    data = df %>% select(-species),
    importance = "permutation"
  )
})

# Extract variable importance
importance_dfs <- imap(rf_models, function(model, sp) {
  if (is.null(model)) return(NULL)
  importance_values <- model$variable.importance
  data.frame(
    Species = sp,
    Variable = names(importance_values),
    Importance = importance_values
  )
}) %>% compact()

# Combine and plot
combined_importance <- bind_rows(importance_dfs)

ggplot(combined_importance, aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance), y = Importance)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Variable Importance by Species (Correlation Filtered)",
    x = "Variables",
    y = "Importance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("./graphics/GoM_RF_Variable_Importance_By_Species_Corr_Filtered.png", width = 10, height = 8)
```

```{r}
## this model takes a long time to run
tic()
brm_model_interact <- brm(
  survival ~ species * MCMT + species * DD5_an + species * CMD_an,
  data = assessed2,
  family = Beta(),
  prior = c(
    prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"),

)

# Extract conditional effects
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# Define a function to process each year
process_period <- function(year) {
  assessed %>%
    filter(PERIOD == year, Planted_year == year) %>%
    mutate(
      CMI_class = case_when(
        CMI_an < -30 ~ "Extreme Drought",
        CMI_an < -20 ~ "Severe Drought",
        CMI_an < -10 ~ "Moderate Drought",
        CMI_an < 0 ~ "Mild Drought",
        TRUE ~ "Non-Drought"
      ),
      CMI_class = factor(CMI_class, levels = c("Extreme Drought","Severe Drought", "Moderate Drought","Mild Drought", "Non-Drought")),
      CMI_class = relevel(CMI_class, ref = "Non-Drought"),
      PERIOD = year  # keep track of the year
    )      %>% 
    mutate(
      CMD_year = CMD_an,
      DD5_year = DD5_an,
      MCMT_year = MCMT,
      CMI_Year = CMI_an)
}

# Apply to all unique PERIODs and combine
assessed_all_years <- map_dfr(unique(assessed$PERIOD), process_period)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ranger)
library(ggplot2)
factors <- c("species", 'CMD_an', 'DD5_an', 'MCMT', 'CMI_an', 'SHM', 'AHM', 'bFFP', 'PAS_an', 'DD18_an', 'MAP', 'MAT', 'DDsub0_sm', 'DDsub0_sp','Eref_an', 'EXT', 'Tmin_sm', 'Tmax_sm', 'Tmin_sp')# 'EMT', 
# Filter and preprocess

  filter(PERIOD == "1961_1990") %>%
  select(survival, species, factors) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(
    survival = round(survival * 100, 0),
    species = as.factor(species)
  )

# Split by species
species_list <- split(assessed.rf, assessed.rf$species)

# Fit RF model for each species
rf_models <- map(species_list, ~ ranger(
  survival ~ .,
  data = select(.x, -species),
  importance = "permutation"
))

# Extract variable importance
importance_dfs <- imap(rf_models, function(model, sp) {
  importance_values <- model$variable.importance
  data.frame(
    Species = sp,
    Variable = names(importance_values),
    Importance = importance_values
  )
})

# Combine and plot
combined_importance <- bind_rows(importance_dfs)

ggplot(combined_importance, aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance), y = Importance)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Variable Importance by Species",
    x = "Variables",
    y = "Importance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# ordinal logistic regression
library(MASS)
assessed$performance <- factor(assessed$performance, levels = c("Fail", "Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Excellent"), ordered = TRUE)
model <- polr(performance ~ Planted_year, data = assessed, Hess = TRUE)
summary(model)

assessed$score <- case_when(
  assessed$performance == "Fail" ~ 1,
  assessed$performance == "Poor" ~ 2,
  assessed$performance == "Fair" ~ 3,
  assessed$performance == "Good" ~ 4,
  assessed$performance == "Excellent" ~ 5
)

# For parametric comparison
anova_result <- aov(score ~ Planted_year, data = assessed)
summary(anova_result)

# For non-parametric comparison
kruskal.test(score ~ Planted_year, data = assessed)

lm_model <- lm(mean_vig ~ Planted_year, data = assessed)
summary(lm_model)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(lm_model)
## is there differential performance between planting year?
lm_model2 <- lm(mean_vig ~ Planted_year + species, data = assessed)
summary(lm_model2)
```

```{r}
##Summary of GoM trials
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(gt)
gom.trials <- fread("./clean_data/gom_trials_compiled.csv")
# Step 1: Create the main summary table
gom.trials.summary <- gom.trials %>%
  group_by(species, year_established) %>%
  tally(name = "n") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year_established,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 2: Reorder year columns numerically
year_cols <- sort(setdiff(names(gom.trials.summary), "species"))

gom.trials.summary <- gom.trials.summary %>%
  select(species, all_of(year_cols)) %>%
  mutate(Total_Trials = rowSums(across(all_of(year_cols)))) %>%
  relocate(Total_Trials, .after = last_col()) %>%
  arrange(species)

# Step 3: Create a summary row for column totals
column_totals <- gom.trials.summary %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(year_cols), sum)) %>%
  mutate(
    species = "Total",
    Total_Trials = sum(across(all_of(year_cols)))
  ) %>%
  select(names(gom.trials.summary))  # ensure column order matches

# Step 4: Bind the summary row to the bottom
gom.trials.summary <- bind_rows(gom.trials.summary, column_totals)

# Step 5: Render with gt
gt::gt(gom.trials.summary) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "GoM Trial Summary by Species and Year Established",
    subtitle = "Number of Trials per Species per Year"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(decimals = 0) %>%
  cols_label(
    species = "Species",
    Total_Trials = "Total Trials"
  ) %>%
  opt_align_table_header("left") %>% gtsave(filename = "./graphics/GoM_trial_summary_by_species_year2.png")

fwrite(gom.trials.summary, "./clean_data/GoM_trial_summary_by_species_year.csv")
```

Assessed trial performance by year
```{r}
assessed <- fread( "./clean_data/GoM_assessed_trials_2023_24.csv")
# Prepare data with counts and percentages
performance_summary <- assessed %>% filter(species %in% c("Cw", "Fd", "Lw", "Pw", "Py")) %>% drop_na %>% 
  count(species, performance, Planted_year) %>%
  group_by(species, Planted_year) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(performance = factor(performance,
                              levels = c("Excellent", "Good", "Fair", "Poor", "Fail"),
                              ordered = TRUE))

# Stacked bar plot with counts and percentage labels
ggplot(performance_summary, aes(x = species, y = n, fill = performance)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(percent), "%")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3, color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Performance Distribution by Species in GoM Assessed Trials planted 2023-24",
       x = "Species",
       y = "Count of Trials",
       fill = "Performance") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Excellent" = "darkgreen",
                               "Good" = "lightgreen",
                               "Fair" = "yellow",
                               "Poor" = "orange",
                               "Fail" = "red")) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")+
  facet_wrap(~Planted_year)

ggsave("./graphics/GoM_assessed_trials_performance_2024_25.png", width = 10, height = 6)
```

```{r}
gom.assessed <- fread("./clean_data/GoM_assessed_trials_2023_24.csv")
gom.assessed.sf <- st_as_sf(gom.assessed, coords = c("Block_long", "Block_lat"), crs = 4326)

# Define performance levels and colors
performance_levels <- c("Fail", "Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Excellent")
performance_colors <- c(
  "Fail" = "red",
  "Poor" = "orange",
  "Fair" = "yellow",
  "Good" = "green",
  "Excellent" = "purple"
)
 sp = "Cw"
for (sp in unique(gom.sf$species)) {
  gom_data <- gom.sf %>% filter(species == sp)
  tree_data <- tree.sf %>% filter(species == sp)
  assessed_data <- gom.assessed.sf %>%
    filter(species == sp) %>%
    mutate(performance = factor(performance, levels = performance_levels))

  # Apply jitter to assessed_data coordinates
  jittered_coords <- st_coordinates(assessed_data) +
    matrix(runif(nrow(assessed_data) * 2, -0.03, 0.03), ncol = 2)
  assessed_data_jittered <- st_as_sf(
    cbind(assessed_data, jittered_coords),
    coords = c("X", "Y"),
    crs = 4326
  )

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = provmap, fill = "grey90", color = "black") +
    geom_sf(data = tree_data, color = "grey50", size = 1, alpha = 0.8, shape = 1) +
    geom_sf(data = gom_data, color = "grey20", size = 1, alpha = 0.8, shape = 15) +
    geom_sf(data = assessed_data_jittered, aes(color = performance), size = 3, shape = 17, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_color_manual(values = performance_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    coord_sf(xlim = st_bbox(provmap)[c("xmin", "xmax")],
             ylim = st_bbox(provmap)[c("ymin", "ymax")],
             expand = FALSE) +
    theme_minimal()+
    labs(
      title = paste("Tree Plot Locations for", sp),
      subtitle = "Species Distribution with Climate Data and Assessed Performance",
      color = "Performance"
    )

  ggsave(filename = paste0("./graphics/map_", sp, ".png"), plot = p, width = 8, height = 6)
}
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Create a data frame of shape codes
shape_df <- data.frame(
  shape = 0:25,
  x = rep(1:6, length.out = 26),
  y = rep(5:1, each = 6, length.out = 26)
)

# Plot the shape codes
ggplot(shape_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = factor(shape)), size = 5, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label = shape), vjust = -1.5, size = 4) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shape_df$shape) +
  theme_void() +
  ggtitle("ggplot2 Shape Codes (0–25)")
```
